newsitem.title: USA: Texas priest retires after sex abuse case comments.
newsitem.headline: Texas priest retires after sex abuse case comments.

text.p: A senior Dallas priest who said parents shared responsibility for the sexual abuse of 11 altar boys by another priest has retired after a public outcry over his comments, officials said on Tuesday.

Monsignor Robert Rehkemper resigned as pastor of the All Saints Catholic Church on Monday, becoming the first Dallas diocese official to step down after a jury last month ordered it to pay a record $119.6 million in damages to the abused former altar boys.

The case has left the diocese in disarray and its troubles multiplied when Rehkemper, 73, said parents of the 11 boys who were allegedly abused hundreds of times by former priest Rudolph Kos were more responsible than the church for letting it happen.

"They more properly should have known because they're close to the kids. I don't want to judge them one way or the other, but it doesn't appear they were very concerned about their kids," he told The Dallas Morning News earlier this month.
He also had words of criticism for the victims. "They knew what was right and what was wrong ... It's hard for me to believe why they kept quiet for so long."
One of the 11 victims committed suicide in 1992. His parents joined the 10 other boys in their civil lawsuit.
Bishop Charles Grahmann, the top diocese official, said he did not ask for Rehkemper's resignation but added that the priest's controversial comments did not reflect the diocese's sentiments.
"His interview caused me to spend a good week deep in reflective prayer," Grahmann told The Dallas Morning News.
A Dallas jury decided last month that the diocese was guilty of gross negligence for allowing Kos access to the altar boys despite receiving several warnings about him.
It also said church officials tried to cover up key information in the case when the boys came forward to complain in 1992. Grahmann has said the church will appeal the verdict.
Kos was suspended when the boys complained and now faces criminal charges. Rehkemper was vicar general during the 11 years that Kos allegedly abused the boys.
